cf.title: enhancing pg_basebackup speeds up to ~23Gbps (small fixes + io_uring/Direct I/O)

input.subject: enhancing pg_basebackup speeds up to ~23Gbps (small fixes + io_uring/Direct I/O)

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal, and a committer is already reviewing the server-side buffer and fadvise patches. The surviving objections are fixable design points on the client side: the exported libpq function (replication-ondisk-1), the `blackhole` rename (standards-compat-1), and Direct I/O on by default with no stated fallback (replication-ondisk-3, standards-compat-3). demand-1 asks for an io_uring measurement without MPTCP. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 15 messages are visible.

brief.title: Speed up pg_basebackup with buffer, fadvise, libpq and io_uring changes
brief.problem: pg_basebackup tops out at about 10-15 Gbps because one core does all the work on each side, with CPU spent on small pread() calls, an extra libpq memcpy and buffered writes. Incremental backups read changed blocks one at a time, so kernel readahead over-reads scattered blocks. The users are operators backing up large clusters on fast networks and storage.
brief.proposed_design: The series keeps the single-threaded, single-connection design. It adds benchmarking targets and a throughput message, raises SINK_BUFFER_LENGTH to 256 kB with short-read retry and a sendFile()/sendRelFile() split, and adds posix_fadvise hints (SEQUENTIAL for full, WILLNEED windows for incremental). On the client side it drops stdio, preallocates files, adds a no-copy libpq receive call, and adds io_uring Direct I/O writes.
user_visible_surface: pg_basebackup --target value blackhole renamed to server-blackhole, also in the BASE_BACKUP protocol TARGET option docs.
New pg_basebackup --target value client-blackhole that receives and discards the backup.
Verbose "base backup completed" message now reports average MB/s.
New exported libpq function PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() (exports.txt entry 212).
Environment variable PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO to turn off Direct I/O; liburing becomes a client build dependency.
author_claims: The full series with MPTCP gives about 1.85x on AWS (about 1610 to 2975 MB/s).
A 256 kB sink buffer raises loopback throughput from about 3.1 to 5.5 GB/s.
Removing the libpq copy takes pg_basebackup from 2.4 to about 5.5 GB/s on localhost without disk writes.
Incremental fadvise prefetch is about 9.8x faster at 14% delta, falling to 1.2x at 57%, by avoiding wasted kernel readahead.
Tar output with Direct I/O needs posix_fallocate(); without it throughput drops to 410 MB/s versus about 2400 MB/s.
brief.thread_state: Heikki Linnakangas reviewed the buffer increase, found short-read and truncation races, and posted a refactor that Jakub merged into 0005; Gustavo William co-authors the incremental fadvise patch. Patches 0007-0011 (stdio, fallocate, libpq API, io_uring) have no review in the thread.
unclear: The patches do not say whether renaming blackhole breaks scripts or older clients, or whether the old name stays as an alias.
Nothing says how io_uring support is detected at build time, or how pg_basebackup behaves on non-Linux platforms.
PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() has no documentation hunk in libpq.sgml, and no review of whether it belongs in the public libpq API.
The MPTCP patch is attached but said to belong in its own thread; its place in this CommitFest entry is not stated.
The patches do not say how Direct I/O behaves on filesystems that reject O_DIRECT or need other alignment.

prior_attempts.title: parallel backup
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P17 sped up base backup with parallel workers and connections. This proposal keeps the single-threaded, single-connection design and cuts per-byte CPU and I/O cost instead.

objections.title: New public libpq symbol for a single in-tree consumer
objections.failure_scenario: A driver author finds PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() in libpq-fe.h, keeps the returned pointer across a later libpq call, and gets COPY data overwritten when libpq refills or moves its input buffer. The corruption is silent. Once exports.txt entry 212 ships, the project cannot remove or change the function without an ABI break.
objections.argument: Patch 0009 adds the function to exports.txt and libpq-fe.h, with no libpq.sgml hunk. The returned buffer is valid only until the next call, which ties callers to libpq's internal buffer handling. The commit message names pg_basebackup as the only consumer, and patches 0007-0011 have no review in the thread. A committer would likely ask for a frontend-private route, or for a documented API that other COPY consumers would use.
objections.author_must_show: Why must this be an exported libpq function instead of a frontend-private interface, and which buffer lifetime rules will the documentation promise?

critic.reasoning: The exports.txt hunk adds entry 212 and the patch has no libpq.sgml hunk. The commit message ties the returned data to libpq's internal buffer until the next call, and nobody in the thread reviewed this patch.

objections.title: io_uring Direct I/O benefit shown only above single-flow TCP limits
objections.failure_scenario: A packager adds liburing as a client build dependency and users get the Direct I/O path, but on links under about 15 Gbps they see no speedup. In run i2, without MPTCP, throughput fell from 1870 to 1695 MB/s. Every build carries the dependency and the PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO switch, while only users on very fast links gain.
objections.argument: Message #1 measures the 0009 gain only with MPTCP, which is not part of this entry and belongs in its own thread. Without MPTCP, run f already saturates the link at 1818 MB/s before 0009. The author's own table [3] puts single-flow TCP at 1-10 Gbps for most environments. That leaves a small group who can use the io_uring path, while the build dependency and the extra code path land on everyone.
objections.author_must_show: Which users today get more than about 15 Gbps on one TCP flow without MPTCP, and what does 0009 give them on that path alone?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 shows the io_uring gain only with MPTCP (i1), and run f already saturates the link without it. Table [3] lists LAN flows on physical servers as CPU-limited, so "1-10 Gbps for most environments" overstates it, but the missing non-MPTCP measurement stands.

objections.title: Renaming the blackhole target breaks scripts and mixed-version backups
objections.failure_scenario: An operator's benchmark script runs `pg_basebackup --target=blackhole` and fails after upgrade. A new pg_basebackup running `-t server-blackhole` against a Postgres 15-19 server sends TARGET 'server-blackhole', which the older server rejects. An older client sending 'blackhole' to a new server fails the same way.
objections.argument: Patch 0001 changes the TARGET value in protocol.sgml and in the pg_basebackup docs, and its commit message mentions no alias. pg_basebackup is expected to work against older servers, and BASE_BACKUP TARGET values are part of the replication protocol. The rename is cosmetic, because adding `client-blackhole` does not require removing `blackhole`.
objections.author_must_show: Will the server keep accepting `blackhole` as an alias, and how does a new pg_basebackup choose the spelling when connected to a pre-20 server?

critic.reasoning: Patch 0001 changes the TARGET value in protocol.sgml and basebackup_target.c, and its commit message names no alias. pg_basebackup passes the target name to the server, so both mixed-version directions fail as described.

objections.title: Direct I/O backup writes lack a defined fallback
objections.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades the client and points pg_basebackup -D at a filesystem that rejects O_DIRECT or needs a different alignment, such as some NFS or tmpfs setups. The backup fails partway, or writes take an untested path. The operator finds out during a scheduled backup run.
objections.argument: Patch 0010 makes io_uring Direct I/O the default for larger files. The only control is the PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO environment variable, which is undocumented. The material gives a buffered fallback only for the tar path when posix_fallocate fails (message #1). It does not say what happens when open(O_DIRECT) or an aligned write fails, or how non-Linux builds without liburing behave. These are the writes that produce the user's backup.
objections.author_must_show: When O_DIRECT or io_uring is unavailable or rejected at run time, does pg_basebackup fall back to buffered writes on every platform, and how is that tested?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 describes a buffered fallback only for the tar path when preallocation is not possible. The material says nothing about a rejected O_DIRECT open, alignment failures, or builds without liburing.

objections.title: Direct I/O control is an environment variable, not an option
objections.failure_scenario: After upgrade, an operator writes backups to a filesystem that rejects O_DIRECT or needs different alignment. The only documented way to turn off Direct I/O is PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO, which is not visible in `--help` or the existing scripts. The operator finds this only when the backup fails or runs slowly.
objections.argument: Patch 0010 turns on io_uring Direct I/O for large files by default and adds PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO, described in message #1 as "for experimenting". pg_basebackup controls client write behaviour with options such as --no-sync, so an environment variable departs from that practice. The proposal does not say how a build without liburing, or a non-Linux build, behaves.
objections.author_must_show: What happens on filesystems that reject O_DIRECT and on builds without liburing, and why is Direct I/O not controlled by a pg_basebackup option?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 introduces PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO only "for experimenting", while Direct I/O is on by default for larger files. The material shows no pg_basebackup option and no documentation for turning it off, so the consistency point stands.

other_surviving.title: Second Linux-only write path in pg_basebackup with no reviewer
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user runs pg_basebackup -Ft to a filesystem that rejects O_DIRECT or where posix_fallocate() is emulated, and throughput falls or the write fails on a path that buildfarm animals without liburing never run. A later astreamer change fixes only the buffered path, and nothing fails on non-Linux CI.
other_surviving.argument: Patches 0010-0011 add io_uring Direct I/O writes beside the buffered path, with a separate tar fallback and an environment variable, PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO, in place of a documented option. Message #1 shows how fragile this is: 0010 was needed because 0009 cut tar output to 410MB/s. Only the server-side patches got review, from Heikki (messages #6-#13), and nobody in the thread has engaged on 0007-0011. The backend already links liburing for AIO, which lowers the dependency cost, but the second frontend code path is new.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How are io_uring support and O_DIRECT capability detected at build and run time, and who will review and maintain the second write path?

critic.reasoning: The series adds a Linux-only write path beside the buffered one, and the material does not say how builds without liburing compile or test it. The missing review of 0007-0011 is a committability matter and must not count against the design.

refuted.title: New exported libpq function lacks documentation and a stable contract
refuted.failure_scenario: A driver author finds PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() in libpq-fe.h and starts using it. They keep the returned pointer past the next libpq call, or expect a trailing NUL as PQgetCopyData() gives, and read freed or overwritten memory. Removing or changing the symbol later breaks every binary linked against it.
refuted.argument: Patch 0009 adds export number 212 but has no libpq.sgml hunk. The commit message says the buffer is valid only until the next call and is not NUL-terminated, which differs from PQgetCopyData(). A name containing "Internal" in the public API conflicts with the existing naming. No one in the thread reviewed 0009, although message #1 notes pg_basebackup is the only consumer.
refuted.author_must_show: What is the documented contract of PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf(), and why must it be a public export instead of a function private to pg_basebackup?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same missing contract and ABI commitment more exactly.

refuted.title: Renaming the BASE_BACKUP target breaks mixed-version use
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs a new pg_basebackup with -t server-blackhole against a v19 server, and the old server rejects the unknown target. A script or third-party tool that sends TARGET 'blackhole' to a new server also fails. Both fail at the first run after the upgrade.
refuted.argument: Patch 0001 changes the documented TARGET value in protocol.sgml. pg_basebackup normally works against older servers. Neither the commit message nor the docs mention an alias for 'blackhole' or a client-side mapping by server version. Keeping 'blackhole' as an accepted alias on the server side would avoid the break, since only the client-side target is new.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the server keep accepting 'blackhole', and what does a new pg_basebackup send to a pre-rename server when given server-blackhole?

refuted.title: New public libpq function shaped for pg_basebackup only
refuted.failure_scenario: A driver author finds PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() in libpq-fe.h and uses it in a COPY TO client. Later a libpq change to input-buffer handling breaks the rule that data stays valid until the next call, and the driver silently reads overwritten bytes. The project cannot remove the export without breaking that driver.
refuted.argument: Patch 0009 adds entry 212 to exports.txt, which commits libpq to the symbol and its semantics for good. Message #1 justifies it with "pg_basebackup is the only consumer", so the API fits one caller. It ties callers to libpq's internal buffer lifetime, with no libpq.sgml hunk and no review in the thread. A committer would likely ask whether a frontend-private path or a general, documented zero-copy COPY API would serve better.
refuted.author_must_show: Why must this be an exported libpq symbol, and what documented contract about buffer lifetime would libpq keep for other callers for good?

refuted.title: Renaming the blackhole target breaks cross-version clients and scripts
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs benchmark scripts with --target=blackhole against an upgraded server, or a new pg_basebackup sends TARGET 'server-blackhole' to an older server. Both fail with an unknown-target error, and the operator finds out only when the run aborts.
refuted.argument: Patch 0001 changes the BASE_BACKUP TARGET value in protocol.sgml and the pg_basebackup option, and the prose shows no alias for the old name. pg_basebackup supports older servers, so the rename affects both directions. The gain is a clearer name for a testing feature, which is small next to a protocol-visible break.
refuted.author_must_show: Will the server keep accepting 'blackhole' as an alias, and how will the new client talk to servers that only know the old name?

refuted.title: client-blackhole overlaps with existing tar-to-stdout discard
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator who wants server plus network throughput without local writes can run `pg_basebackup -Ft -D - -X fetch > /dev/null` today. The patch adds a permanent `--target` value for much the same measurement. It also adds a flag that every future change to the astreamer extractors in astreamer_file.c must respect.
refuted.argument: pg_basebackup already writes a tar stream to stdout with `-D -`, limited to clusters without extra tablespaces and without WAL streaming. Message #1 presents client-blackhole as a way to measure each stage, but does not compare it with the stdout route. client-blackhole also exercises the plain-format extractor and works with tablespaces, which stdout cannot. The proposal does not say whether that extra coverage is the purpose, and a committer would likely ask whether it justifies a user-visible testing-only option.
refuted.author_must_show: What does client-blackhole measure that `pg_basebackup -Ft -D - -X fetch > /dev/null` cannot, and do users other than benchmark authors need it?

critic.reasoning: The objection itself says the stdout route cannot cover tablespaces, WAL streaming or the plain-format extractor, which is the path the benchmarks in message #1 use. A test-only target also follows the existing `blackhole` target.

refuted.title: Permanent public libpq function with one stated consumer
refuted.failure_scenario: PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() becomes export 212. Driver and extension authors then depend on a buffer that is valid only until the next call. Once one of them relies on it, libpq cannot change its input buffer handling without breaking them.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says pg_basebackup is the only consumer and justifies the copy removal by that. The exports.txt hunk makes the function part of the libpq ABI, but the patch has no libpq.sgml entry and no other client in the thread asks for it. The cost of keeping the ABI falls on every libpq user and maintainer, and the gain shown is for one bundled tool. Patches 0007-0011 have no review in the thread.
refuted.author_must_show: Which clients other than pg_basebackup need a no-copy COPY receive call, and why can pg_basebackup not get the same gain without a new exported libpq symbol?

refuted.title: Renaming the blackhole target has a cost and no requester
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator's benchmark script runs pg_basebackup --target=blackhole, or a third-party tool sends TARGET 'blackhole' in BASE_BACKUP. After upgrade the target name is rejected, and they find out when the script fails.
refuted.argument: Patch 0001 renames the documented value in both pg_basebackup and the protocol docs, and does not say whether the old name stays as an alias. The thread gives no user request for the rename. Its only purpose is to make room for a name for client-blackhole, which could be added under a new name next to the existing one.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can client-blackhole not be added while blackhole keeps working, at least as an alias?

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-3: Direct I/O backup writes lack a defined fallback

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The series rewrites the server-side base backup read path in basebackup.c, including short-read and truncation handling.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 renames the BASE_BACKUP TARGET value `blackhole` to `server-blackhole` in protocol.sgml.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The libpq patch adds PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() as exports.txt entry 212.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The target rename makes a new pg_basebackup and an older server disagree on the name, in both directions.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The series adds a Linux-only io_uring Direct I/O write path, a liburing client dependency and a permanent libpq export.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The 256 kB sink buffer and the fadvise calls change the read path of every base backup.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: see objection demand-1: io_uring Direct I/O benefit shown only above single-flow TCP limits

questions: Why must PQgetCopyDataInternalBuf() be an exported libpq function instead of a frontend-private interface, and which buffer lifetime rules will libpq.sgml promise?
Will the server keep accepting `blackhole` as an alias, and what does a new pg_basebackup send to a pre-20 server for `-t server-blackhole`?
When the target filesystem rejects O_DIRECT, or the build has no liburing, does pg_basebackup fall back to buffered writes on every platform?
What does the io_uring Direct I/O patch gain on a single TCP flow without MPTCP, given that run i2 was slower than run h3?
Why is Direct I/O on by default and controlled by the PG_BASEBACKUP_NODIO environment variable instead of a documented pg_basebackup option?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas reviewed the server-side buffer and short-read patches. The client-side patches need someone who knows the libpq API and ABI rules, and someone who knows the pg_basebackup astreamer code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent libpq export, for a Linux-only Direct I/O write path that produces users' backups, and for the reworked short-read handling in basebackup.c.
committability.author_follow_up: The author merged the reviewer's refactor into the series and posted new versions up to message #15, after a rebase in October.

priority.reason: The server-side buffer and fadvise patches have measured gains, an independent report of slow incremental backups in message #2, and active committer review, so they can go ahead on their own. The libpq export and the io_uring patches span libpq, fe_utils and pg_basebackup and need their own design answers first.

provisional_note: Without the code, the short-read and truncation handling in basebackup.c, the buffer lifetime of the new libpq call, and the Direct I/O alignment and error paths could not be checked. Only 3 of 15 messages were visible, so later answers may exist.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent pg_basebackup running as root
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_basebackup refuse to run as root (except for --help/--version), matching the existing checks in initdb, pg_ctl and pg_upgrade, so it cannot create root-owned files in a data directory that the postmaster could not use. The change was not to be backpatched, as it alters behavior.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed by Michael Paquier and then reverted after a separate discussion that is linked but not included in the visible messages. The visible messages do not show why.

precedents_retrieved.title: base backup client as auxiliary backend process
precedents_retrieved.summary: The postmaster starts an auxiliary process that takes a base backup from the primary when it finds a basebackup.signal file in a minimal data directory created by initdb, then continues startup in standby mode. Connection settings come from postgresql.conf, so setting up a standby no longer needs pg_basebackup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry because he could not finish it, and said the order of startup actions in postmaster.c needed more thinking. Andres Freund's review had questioned the polling wait loop in PostmasterMain, missing error and signal handling in the base backup process, the handling of shutdown during the backup, and putting the backup code in libpqwalreceiver.c. Some refactoring parts were committed separately.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Unsurprisingly, the sequencing of startup actions in postmaster.c is
extremely tricky and needs more thinking.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revise documentation on base backups
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites the base backup section of the continuous archiving documentation (Section 24.3.2), written by a newcomer who followed it as a tutorial. The author also points out that the manual has no fixed term for the directory that holds postgresql.conf.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only message is the author's submission, which asks experienced readers to check the rewrite for technical accuracy, and no reply is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Windows pg_basebackup unable to create >2GB pg_wal.tar tarballs ("could not close file: Invalid argument" when creating pg_wal.tar of size ~ 2^31 bytes)
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, pg_basebackup in tar mode fails with "could not close file: Invalid argument" when pg_wal.tar grows past 2^31 bytes, because off_t, lseek() and ftruncate() are 32-bit there. A proof-of-concept patch redirects lseek() to _lseeki64() so the WAL tar file can exceed 2 GiB.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message discusses how to back-patch the fix, including an ftruncate() replacement, and nobody objects to it. The entry was withdrawn three days later, and no message gives a reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Application name for pg_basebackup, pg_receivewal and pg_recvlogical
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an -a / --appname command line switch to pg_basebackup, pg_receivewal and pg_recvlogical to set the application name of their connection. The stated use case was letting pg_receivewal connect as a synchronous client listed in synchronous_standby_names.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers noted that the application name can already be set through the environment variable or the application_name parameter in the connection string passed with -d, so a new switch was not needed. The patch was marked rejected in the CommitFest app on that basis, and the author agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think we need a new comand line switch for it.

precedents_retrieved.summary: Fix base backup checksum verification for random or zero page headers

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_basebackup to adjust existing data directory permissions
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_basebackup was proposed to change the permissions of an existing target data directory to the required permissions, as initdb does, so that the postmaster can start on the resulting backup. The discussion later extended this to a -g {inherit|none|group} option controlling group access on the backup, including changes to BASE_BACKUP so that tar-mode backups carry the chosen permissions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on the desired behavior. Peter Eisentraut and David Steele considered the proposed options too complicated for a problem the user can fix by changing permissions, while others wanted the current behavior changed; the author's tally showed support and opposition. Alvaro Herrera noted the discussion was inconclusive and the patch dormant, and after a further idle period the entry was closed as returned with little useful feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There's been at lot of
discussion but it doesn't seem conclusive; it doesn't look like we know
what we actually want to do.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_basebackup: add test about zstd compress option
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a test to pg_basebackup's TAP tests that exercises the zstd compression option, later extended to verify the generated files with the zstd binary. A follow-up version refactored the test to cover multiple compression methods (gzip, lz4, zstd) and check output with each respective decompression program.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas pointed out that existing tests in src/bin/pg_verifybackup (008_untar.pl and 009_extract.pl) already cover compressed base backups, and that the only additional scenario the new test could catch was not worth the extra CPU cycles. Ian Lawrence Barwick and the author agreed the test did not add anything, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would be inclined to dismiss that particular scenario as not important
enough to be worth the additional CPU cycles.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reorder tablespaces for streaming basebackups
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed the order of the tar streams sent by the BASE_BACKUP replication command so that the main data directory comes first, which puts backup_label at the beginning of a combined tarball for third-party tools. After review it was narrowed to apply only when WAL is not included, because in fetch mode the WAL files are appended to the main tarball, which must therefore stay last.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fujii Masao pointed out that BASE_BACKUP already sends the start WAL location in its first result set, before any tar data, so reading backup_label early is not needed for that purpose; further information could be added to that result set instead. He also said that running BASE_BACKUP through psql is not a good approach and that a proper client or an extension of pg_basebackup should be used. Michael Paquier agreed that the patch was therefore not useful and proposed dropping it, and the author marked it Rejected as the consensus.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In my first reviews of the patch, I completely forgot the fact that
BASE_BACKUP does send the start LSN of the backup in the first result
set, so the patch proposed is actually rather useless because the data
you are looking for is already at hand.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the patch to check if we've reached end-of-backup also when doing crash recovery, and throw an error if not.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert the patch to check if we've reached end-of-backup also when doing crash recovery, and throw an error if not. hubert depesz lubaczewski pointed out that that situation also happens in the crash recovery following a system crash that happens during an online backup.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert the patch to check if we've reached end-of-backup also when doing
crash recovery, and throw an error if not. hubert depesz lubaczewski pointed

roaster_notes.note: The only precedent, [P17], has no recorded reason, so no earlier rejection reason can be tested against this proposal. Message #1 links the old parallel-backup thread and keeps the single-connection design to avoid its open questions, but the thread does not say what those questions were.

The proposal changes no heap, WAL, catalog or replication-slot state. The server-side read and fadvise changes are under active review by Heikki in messages #6-#14, so this angle does not object to them.

The series does not change who may run a base backup or what that role can read; the server work still runs under the existing replication privilege, and the fadvise window is bounded by maintenance_io_concurrency and io_combine_limit. Client-side changes (client-blackhole, fallocate from tar sizes, Direct I/O, the new libpq call) act only for the client user, against a server it already trusts, so I found no security or privilege objection.
The server-side patches 0004-0006 have engaged committer review and can be committed on their own, so this angle raises nothing against them.

The other parts have no existing equivalent I can name. Postgres has no zero-copy COPY receive call, no fadvise prefetch for incremental reads, and no Direct I/O path in pg_basebackup, so the extension and existing-feature angle finds nothing further.

Demand for faster full and incremental backups is real. Gustavo independently reported slow incremental backups in message #2, and Heikki is engaged on 0004-0005. These objections concern the client-side pieces (0001, 0009-0011), not the server-side read path.

warnings: synthesis said NEEDS-COMMITTER-EYES but listed a level 1b objection (demand-1); changed to NEEDS-DESIGN-DISCUSSION
